facts.fact: The Information Regulator imposed its first fine, R5 million, on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development for breaching POPIA, according to ITWeb quoting the Regulator.

The Regulator also fined the Department of Basic Education R5 million, and the Electoral Commission and Lancet Laboratories R100,000 each, both paid; the document gives no dates for these (published 2026-09-02).

The Regulator fined Blouberg Local Municipality R500,000; the municipality did not pay, the Regulator went to court to confirm it, and the court reduced it to R250,000 as too high for a first offence; the document gives no date (published 2026-09-02).
A R100,000 fine on FT Rams Consulting for direct marketing is being processed under section 109 of POPIA, per the Regulator's executive for POPIA (document published 2026-09-02).

ITWeb reports that the Regulator's enforcement powers came into force on 1 July 2021 after a year-long compliance grace period, and that POPIA provides fines up to R10 million and up to 10 years' imprisonment.
